title: Cool-Down Walk and Stretch
description: Two slow laps and a guided stretch circle bring heart rates down, loosen tired muscles and let the coach close the session with a calm, positive message.

content.objective: Bring heart rates down gradually, loosen the muscles used in practice and finish the session calmly.
content.setup: Players form a loose circle at the top of the key, an arm's length apart, with the coach standing in the middle where everyone can see and hear.
content.organization: One circle for the whole team (up to about 20 players). With a bigger group, make two circles and ask an assistant to lead the second one.
instructions: Walk two slow laps around the court, breathing in through the nose for four steps and out through the mouth for four steps.
Gather in the circle. Hold each stretch for 20 seconds without bouncing: calves, quadriceps, hamstrings, hip flexors and groin.
Finish with the shoulders and arms: a cross-body stretch, a triceps stretch and slow shoulder rolls forward and back.
Stand or sit quietly for one minute while the coach names two positives from today and one focus for the next session.
coachingPoints: Stretch to mild tension only, never to pain.
Breathe slowly and exhale as you move deeper into a stretch.
Use the quiet minute to reinforce what went well.
commonMistakes: Rushing the stretches to leave early.
Bouncing in a stretch instead of holding still.
Talking over the coach's closing message.
content.safety: Anyone with a sore joint or muscle skips that stretch and tells the coach.
progressions: Add a guided breathing pattern (four counts in, six out) for the last minute.
regressions: For younger players, shorten each hold to 10 seconds and lead by demonstration.
variations: Let a different player lead one stretch each session.
Play calm background music to set the tone.
